Over time, the volume will even out, but on any given day or any given week, the volume for Pools in the same region with the same saturation can vary by large amounts if they were "unlucky."

The biggest differences are seen between regions.  Traffic is gated between regions.  If my Pool is in the US, I have no chance to serve traffic from the EU, AP or SA.  The traffic within a region is split between the Pools (thus Nodes) within that region.  But, the rewards are split globally.  So, if one region has significantly more traffic than another region, the Pools in that region will benefit over the Pools in the other region.  This effect is magnified when a region with only a few Pools receives even moderate traffic, since the small number of Pools split that traffic, and on a per Node basis, their volume is outsized compared to the Pools in other regions.  We have seen this in AP the past few days, for example.  We have also seen days with 0 traffic in AP.

If a node earns 10 COPI, delegating it to a pool with a 10% fee gives you 9 COPI and the pool operator 1 COPI; running and self-delegating (your own pool) yields the full 10 COPI to you.

Delegation: you register the node and choose a public pool via the Manage Nodes flow; the pool’s fee (%) is locked for the life of that delegation and applies to performance rewards (see the Node Delegation page). Example: 10 COPI reward × 10% pool fee = 1 COPI to pool, 9 COPI to you. Pools can cap delegations; changing pools requires undelegating and re-delegating (you lose a day of rewards).

Running it yourself: if you run the pool server and delegate to your own pool, the fee is treated as 0%, so you keep the entire reward (10 COPI). Running your own pool also requires additional setup and operational responsibilities (docker, port forwarding, uptime, cache storage) as described on the Pool Server Setup and rewards overview on the In-game Rewards page.
